slides.2.title: Overview of the Six Wine States
slides.2.points.0: 🟠 South Australia (SA): most important state — Barossa Valley, McLaren Vale, Coonawarra
slides.2.points.1: 🟣 Victoria (VIC): densest concentration of regions — Yarra Valley, Heathcote, Rutherglen
slides.2.points.2: 🔵 New South Wales (NSW): Australia's oldest — Hunter Valley, Orange, Riverina
slides.2.points.3: 🟡 Western Australia (WA): boutique-focused — Margaret River, Great Southern
slides.2.points.4: 🔴 Queensland (QLD): northernmost — Granite Belt at altitude
slides.2.points.5: 🟢 Tasmania (TAS): southernmost and coolest — premium sparkling wines
slides.3.title: Southern vs Northern Hemisphere: Opposite Seasons
slides.3.left.label: Australia (Southern Hemisphere)
slides.3.left.points.3: Climate: cooler in the south, warmer in the north
slides.3.right.label: Europe (Northern Hemisphere)
slides.3.right.points.3: Climate: cooler in the north, warmer in the south
slides.4.title: South Australia: Australia's Wine Capital
slides.4.points.0: Produces roughly 50% of all Australian wine (including large irrigated regions)
slides.4.points.1: Most famous: Barossa Valley (Shiraz old vines), Clare Valley (Riesling)
slides.5.title: Lesson Summary
slides.5.points.0: SA produces ~50% of Australian wine; VIC has the most wine regions; NSW is historically significant
slides.5.points.1: Southern Hemisphere harvest is February–April — opposite to Europe
slides.5.points.2: Tasmania is coolest (southernmost); QLD Granite Belt is highest in altitude
